The score function is the vector of the two partial derivatives:

$$
\score(\mu, \sigma^2) =
\begin{pmatrix}
\deriv{\mu}\ell(\mu, \sigma^2) \\
\deriv{\sigma^2}\ell(\mu, \sigma^2)
\end{pmatrix}
$$

For the first entry,
only the last term of $\ell$ depends on $\mu$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\mu}\ell
&= \deriv{\mu}\paren{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi} - \frac{n}{2}\logf{\sigma^2}
 - \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(Gaussian log-likelihood)}\\
&= \deriv{\mu}\paren{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi}} + \deriv{\mu}\paren{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\sigma^2}}
 + \deriv{\mu}\paren{-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}\\
&= 0 + 0 + \deriv{\mu}\paren{-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(derivative of a constant)}\\
&= \deriv{\mu}\paren{-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(drop the zero terms)}\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\deriv{\mu}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n \deriv{\mu}(x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(derivative of a sum is the sum of derivatives)}\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n 2(x_i - \mu)\deriv{\mu}(x_i - \mu)
&& \text{(chain rule, outer function $u^2$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The inner derivative is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\mu}(x_i - \mu)
&= \deriv{\mu} x_i - \deriv{\mu} \mu
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}\\
&= 0 - \deriv{\mu} \mu
&& \text{($x_i$ does not depend on $\mu$)}\\
&= 0 - 1
&& \text{(derivative of $\mu$ with respect to itself)}\\
&= -1
&& \text{(subtract)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the inner derivative back in:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\mu}\ell
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n 2(x_i - \mu) \cdot (-1)
&& \text{(inner derivative is $-1$)}\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n -2(x_i - \mu)
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2} \cdot (-2) \sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)
&& \text{(factor the constant $-2$ out of the sum)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)
&& \text{(multiply the constants)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\sigma^2}\paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i - \sum_{i=1}^n \mu}
&& \text{(split the sum)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\sigma^2}\paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i - n\mu}
&& \text{(sum of $n$ copies of $\mu$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

For the second entry,
write $\sigma^2$ as a single variable $v$, so that $\ell$ contains
$-\frac{n}{2}\log v$ and $-\frac{1}{2}v^{-1}\sum_i (x_i - \mu)^2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\sigma^2}\ell
&= \deriv{\sigma^2}\paren{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi} - \frac{n}{2}\logf{\sigma^2}
 - \frac{1}{2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(Gaussian log-likelihood)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\deriv{\sigma^2}\logf{2\pi} - \frac{n}{2}\deriv{\sigma^2}\logf{\sigma^2}
 - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2 \deriv{\sigma^2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-1}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2} \cdot 0 - \frac{n}{2}\deriv{\sigma^2}\logf{\sigma^2}
 - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2 \deriv{\sigma^2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-1}
&& \text{(derivative of a constant)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\deriv{\sigma^2}\logf{\sigma^2}
 - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2 \deriv{\sigma^2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-1}
&& \text{(drop the zero term)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-1}
 - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2 \deriv{\sigma^2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-1}
&& \text{(derivative of $\log v$)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-1}
 - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2 \paren{-\paren{\sigma^2}^{-2}}
&& \text{(power rule for $v^{-1}$)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-1}
 + \frac{1}{2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(multiply)}
\end{aligned}
$$
